headline: Role-based governance via 4-of-7/3-of-6/3-of-5 multisigs + 1-3 day timelock on upgradeable Globals; T1 actions (pause, upgrade, oracle config) reachable in <7 days

findings.text: daoMultisig (0xd6d4Bcde6c816F17889f1Dd3000aF0261B03a196) is 4-of-7 Gnosis Safe (block 25204116); securityAdmin (0x6b1A78C1943b03086F7Ee53360f9b0672bD60818) 3-of-6 Safe; operationalAdmin (0xCe1cE7c7F436DCc4E28Bc8bf86115514d3DC34E8) 3-of-5 Safe; globalAdmin (0x0D8b2C1F11c5f9cD51de6dB3b256C1e3b0800200) 2-of-3 Safe; permissionsAdmin (0x54b130c704919320E17F4F1Ffa4832A91AB29Dca) Safe; globals singleton (0x804a6F5F667170F545Bf14e5DDB48C70B788390C) exposes governor=0x2eFFf88747EB5a3FF00d4d8d0f0800E306C0426b, operationalAdmin, securityAdmin, setProtocolPause, setImplementation

Globals is upgradeable proxy (setImplementation); PoolManagerFactory and loan factories support upgrade paths; pools non-proxy but manager-controlled; GovernorTimelock is non-proxy role-based controller

Execution path: role holder (PROPOSER_ROLE on GovernorTimelock) → schedule proposal (MIN_DELAY=86400s/1 day, default 3d delay) → execute after delay; arbitrary calls via scheduleCall on Globals also timelocked

Multisigs with reachable control: daoMultisig 4-of-7, securityAdmin 3-of-6, operationalAdmin 3-of-5, globalAdmin 2-of-3; none qualify as Security Council (signer count or unknown insider %); no on-chain token voting
No token-weighted on-chain governance (role-based PROPOSER/EXECUTOR/CANCELLER/ROLE_ADMIN on GovernorTimelock; no votingPeriod/quorum reads); latestProposalId=13
Emergency powers via securityAdmin/operationalAdmin on Globals.setProtocolPause/setContractPause; no explicit time cap; can be indefinite until governance unpause
Highest tier T1 on fast path: setProtocolPause (affects all pools/withdrawals), setImplementation (upgrade fund-holding logic), setPriceOracle (oracle swap); all via <7d timelock + multisig (not SC)

steelman.red: T1 (pause/upgrade/oracle) reachable by 4-of-7 or 3-of-5 multisig with only 1-day min delay and no Security Council safeguards or token veto.
steelman.orange: T1 actions gated behind 1-3 day timelock on role-based GovernorTimelock + Globals; multiple independent multisigs distribute power; no single EOA or 2-of-3 unilateral control.
steelman.green: All T1 paths require multisig approval + explicit timelock delay; upgrade surface is narrow and delayed; no immediate rug path.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because T1 (protocol pause, proxy upgrade, oracle config) is reachable on the uncontested fast path via multisig-controlled timelock with only 1-3 day delay; multisigs fail Security Council criteria and delay <7 days, outweighing the green steel-man of distributed roles and no EOA control.

protocol_metadata.about: Maple Finance provides on-chain secured lending pools for institutional borrowers and liquid yield products (syrupUSDC/USDT) backed by overcollateralized loans. Liquidity providers deposit into ERC-4626 pools or request redemptions via cyclical/queue managers; borrowers access fixed/open-term loans. Role-based governance controls parameters, pauses, upgrades, and oracles through multisig timelocks and upgradeable Globals contract.

headline: Permissionless redeem/withdraw/requestRedeem on pools; protocol-level pause via security/operational multisig on Globals with no visible time cap or frontend gate

findings.text: User-facing exit functions on syrupUSDCPool (0x80ac24aA929eaF5013f6436cdA2a7ba190f5Cc0b): redeem, withdraw, requestRedeem, requestWithdraw, removeShares, convertToExitAssets at block 25204119
No access modifiers or pause guards visible on pool exit functions (no whenNotPaused or onlyRole on redeem/requestRedeem); manager (PoolManager) controls but exits are direct

Globals (0x804a6F5F667170F545Bf14e5DDB48C70B788390C) exposes setProtocolPause(bool), setContractPause(address,bool), setFunctionUnpause; protocolPaused() view=false at block 25204121; pause role held by securityAdmin/operationalAdmin multisigs; no max duration or auto-expiry read
Emergency pause (securityAdmin multisig) and governance pause (via timelock) both route to same Globals functions; no separate time-capped emergency guardian distinguished
requestRedeem/requestWithdraw indicate queued/cyclical redemption (withdrawal-manager-cyclical submodule); max queue duration not read on-chain in this run
No permissionless forced-exit or escape-hatch beyond standard requestRedeem; no admin-signature requirement for user exits
Exit functions directly callable on Etherscan write tab or any wallet (no frontend dependency for on-chain execution)

steelman.red: Globals.setProtocolPause callable by 3-of-6 or 3-of-5 multisig with no time cap can freeze all new requests and potentially claims; indefinite pause reachable without governance vote.
steelman.orange: Core exit functions (redeem/requestRedeem) on individual pools have no pause guard; only broad protocol pause exists and is held by distributed multisigs with timelock path for unpause; queued redemptions provide exit window.
steelman.green: No contract-level whitelist or admin signature required for exits; requestRedeem is permissionless and directly on-chain; pause does not retroactively block already-finalized claims.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because indefinite protocol pause is reachable by multisig (security/operational) without visible time cap or separate governance-only path, but exits remain permissionless on pools and no frontend gate or admin signature blocks user actions; stronger than red due to queued mechanisms and distributed pause holders.

evidence.shows: Pool contract with redeem, withdraw, requestRedeem, requestWithdraw; no paused() or pause guard; manager address surfaced at block 25204119
Globals setProtocolPause, setContractPause, protocolPaused()=false at block 25204121; no max pause duration
withdrawal-manager-cyclical and withdrawal-manager-queue submodules for queued redemptions

unknowns: E3: exact caller restrictions (hasRole or onlyRole on setProtocolPause) not read; assumed multisig from admin addresses
E5: documented max queue duration or daily caps not readable on withdrawal manager contracts in this run

headline: ~100% TVS exposed to Chainlink price feeds + CCIP cross-chain; no live on-chain fallback or sanity checks read; oracles mutable via Globals admin

findings.text: Globals (0x804a6F5F667170F545Bf14e5DDB48C70B788390C) exposes setPriceOracle(address) and price oracles per asset; Chainlink Price Feeds used for syrupUSDC valuation and loan collateral (Chainlink ecosystem page); no on-chain latestAnswer or sanity-check read in this run

MapleCCIPReceiver proxy (0x02B6A75c5D1F430F0614dc5AC8aD5F9D35fbA2c4) and Chainlink CCIP for cross-chain syrupUSDC transfers (Ethereum-Solana); >$500M AUM noted in 2025 integration; Base deployment adds L2 dependency
No deep restaking/LRT nesting; collateral is institutional loans or overcollateralized assets in isolated pools; failure in one pool does not propagate to others
No live fallback (second oracle, rebase bound, or circuit breaker) read in Globals or pools; setPriceOracle is governance-mutable without exit window for users

Globals admin (operational/security multisig via timelock) can swap price oracle address or add new CCIP endpoints without 7-day user exit window; upgrade paths on factories allow new external dependencies
No off-chain oracle committees or validator sets; price feeds are Chainlink decentralized network (not single operator)

steelman.red: Single external oracle provider (Chainlink) with mutable address via admin and no on-chain fallback; CCIP guardian set controls cross-chain TVL; oracle failure or CCIP freeze can impair collateral valuation and withdrawals across all pools.
steelman.orange: Critical dependencies (Chainlink oracles for pricing, CCIP for ~$500M+ cross-chain AUM) exist but are decentralized networks with known mitigations; no governance can hot-swap without timelock; isolated pools limit blast radius; impacted TVS bounded by overcollateralization.
steelman.green: No single-point keeper or bridge with guardian multisig on primary TVL; oracles are standard decentralized feeds; pool isolation and cyclical withdrawals absorb transient failures without principal loss.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because Chainlink price feeds and CCIP cross-chain messaging are material external dependencies (~100% TVS) that can degrade pricing or freeze cross-chain exits if they fail, with governance-mutable oracle surface (A9) and no verified live fallback (A6); stronger than red due to decentralized oracle network and isolated pool design, but weaker than green due to lack of on-chain sanity checks or dual-oracle enforcement.

headline: Permissionless on-chain deposit/redeem/requestRedeem; no contract whitelist or KYC gate; direct Etherscan/wallet access + aggregators; frontend ToS only

findings.text: No onlyWhitelisted, onlyRole, isAccredited, or KYC modifiers on pool entry/exit functions (redeem, requestRedeem, deposit implied via ERC-4626); pools admit unconditionally
No off-chain operator approval required for deposit or requestRedeem; keepers/relayers only for liquidations (permissionless bots); no sequencer or privileged relayer in admission path

Official frontend has standard ToS (sanctions attestation, restricted territories self-certification); no runtime IP geo-blocking or Chainalysis wallet screening confirmed on-chain or in contract reads

Independent paths exist: direct Etherscan write tab on pool addresses, any Web3 wallet (MetaMask), DEX/lending aggregators routing to ERC-4626 pools, third-party frontends; no published SDK required but on-chain accessibility confirmed
No on-chain blocklist or OFAC check in pool or Globals contracts; sanctions enforcement is frontend-only
Read access fully permissionless (anyone can call view methods); write access (deposit/redeem) also permissionless on contracts
ToS on maple.finance references compliance with applicable law and eligibility; no verbatim sanctions clause extracted but standard boilerplate only

steelman.red: Institutional lending products may impose off-chain KYC for borrowers, but even if true it does not gate lender entry/exit on syrup pools or contract level.
steelman.orange: Official UI may have geo-blocking or ToS restrictions, but contracts remain open; however, no third-party frontend or aggregator routing would make it operationally captured.
steelman.green: Contracts are fully permissionless for all user actions (deposit, requestRedeem, redeem); multiple independent on-chain access paths exist (Etherscan, wallets, aggregators); no contract-level admission gate or operator approval.

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because core user actions (deposit, requestRedeem, redeem) are unconditionally admitted by the smart contracts with no whitelist, KYC modifier, or operator approval; independent access via Etherscan and wallets exists regardless of official frontend ToS or any A3-active enforcement.

evidence.shows: No whitelist or role-gated modifiers on redeem/requestRedeem/withdraw at block 25204119; direct callable
syrupUSDC/USDT promoted for individuals/institutions; no on-site KYC wall or geo-banner in overview
Write functions (redeem, requestRedeem) publicly callable without restrictions (inferred from ABI surface)

unknowns: A3: verbatim ToS sanctions clause not extracted due to SPA render; only general compliance language observed

headline: All key contracts (Globals, pools, factories, Safe proxies) bytecode verified on Etherscan via defipunkd; public GitHub maple-labs repos with audits (code-423n4 + 0xMacro 2025)

findings.text: daoMultisig, securityAdmin, operationalAdmin, globalAdmin, GovernorTimelock, Globals proxy+impl, pools, factories all return verified=true or GnosisSafeProxy with ABI from Etherscan in defipunkd reads (blocks 25204116-25204124); implementation resolved for proxies
Source matches public maple-labs/maple-core-v2 and submodules (pool-v2, globals-v2, withdrawal-manager-cyclical); no commit SHA pinned but structure and file contents correspond to deployed ABIs
Audits in protocol.audit_links (code-423n4 2021-04, 2021-12, 2022-03) plus GitHub /audits/0xMacro-Maple-Finance-timelock-Sept-2025.pdf covering GovernorTimelock and core v2 contracts
code-423n4 (recognized competitive audit platform) and 0xMacro (recognized firm) cover deployed contracts; no unknown-firm audits
No material post-audit drift detected in surface reads (upgrade paths, pause functions, roles consistent with audited patterns); recent 2025 audit covers timelock changes
All proxies (Globals, Safes, CCIPReceiver) have verified implementations; no unverified impl case

steelman.red: Some peripheral factories or Base contracts may have older audits or unverified status, but core control and pool contracts are fully covered.
steelman.orange: Audits predate some v2 deployments by >6 months and no differential audit for every upgrade path; minor drift possible in un-audited submodules.
steelman.green: Bytecode verified across all key addresses via live defipunkd/Etherscan; multiple recognized audits including recent GovernorTimelock review; public repos match deployed ABIs with no unverified implementation.

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because every assessed contract (Globals proxy+impl, GovernorTimelock, all multisig proxies, main pools) shows verified bytecode and ABI on defipunkd/Etherscan, public GitHub source corresponds to deployed code, and audits from recognized firms (code-423n4, 0xMacro) cover the current surface with recent timelock review; no unverified implementation or missing audit for core control paths.
